# Help users reach their first useful result

Define the first outcome that matters to the user, such as opening a working preview or saving
a first project. Walk the existing path and record where it asks for information, stalls, or gives
unclear feedback. Distinguish observed friction from hypotheses. Consider both beginners and
users who already know the product.

Use a real action or a working example to teach the next step. Collect only information needed
to proceed. Offer a way to skip optional guidance and reach it again later. In empty states,
explain what belongs there and give a concrete next action. Show specific recovery steps for
validation errors and preserve progress when a flow can be resumed.

Verify first use, skipping guidance, returning to the product, and recovering from an error.
If existing analytics cover the task, compare completion or time to first value using the same
definition before and after the change. Otherwise report the available observations and the
evidence still needed.
